officialName: Indian Institute of Technology (Indian School of Mines) Dhanbad
about: Indian Institute of Technology (Indian School of Mines) Dhanbad traces its roots to 1926, when the British government founded the Indian School of Mines to train mining and geology professionals; it earned deemed-university status in 1967 and became an IIT in 2016. It remains the only IIT with full-fledged mining, petroleum, applied geology and geophysics departments alongside the usual engineering and science disciplines. The Dhanbad campus sits in India's coal belt, and the institute pairs its earth-science legacy with newer programmes in computing, electronics and management.
